old_description: Our engineering, design and quality teams help ensure that our clients get what they want and to the exact specifications outlined. We work closely with clients to help ensure this.
about:
YAPP Automotive USA, Inc., operating as YAPP USA Automotive Systems, Inc., is based in Chattanooga, Tennessee. The company does not publicly disclose its founding year, ownership structure, or founders.

The company designs, engineers, and manufactures automotive fuel system solutions. Its core processes include injection molding, co-extrusion, and a proprietary extrusion blow molding (EBM) technique used to produce multi-layer blow-molded fuel management systems, fuel tanks, fuel transfer systems, and filler pipe systems with molded-in tabs and multi-layer conductivity. Facility size, headcount, and production volumes are not disclosed.

As a Tier 1 supplier, YAPP USA serves major automotive OEMs including General Motors, Volvo, Volkswagen, Ford, Stellantis (FCA), and Nissan, as well as heavy-equipment manufacturer John Deere.

The company emphasizes proactive quality management, a zero-defect policy, and continuous improvement. Its proprietary blow molding process reduces component count and improves product quality, while a culture of innovation drives research and development in advanced materials and technologies.

old_description: “Embrace Your Yoga Journey with Yoganastix: Where Comfort Meets Conscious Design”At Yoganastix,...
about:
Yoganastix operates from Phoenix, Arizona, where it produces activewear and resort wear through cut-and-sew manufacturing. The company does not publicly disclose its founding year, ownership structure, or founder names.

The facility provides design, fabric sourcing, and cut-and-sew production for leggings, goddess pants, kimono robes, bell bottoms, shorts, tops, dresses, and accessories such as scrunchies. It offers private-label manufacturing and custom branding using either its proven Yoganastix styles or client-supplied production-ready files. All items are described as Phoenix-made and sustainably made in Arizona, though facility size, headcount, and annual volume are not published.

Yoganastix serves the activewear, yoga, resort-wear, and eco-fashion markets. Its direct-to-consumer line sells reversible leggings, printed pants, and kimono robes, while the private-label side targets brands seeking domestic cut-and-sew partners for sustainable apparel collections. Travel and lifestyle segments are also referenced in the product assortment.

The company positions itself on domestic, eco-conscious production: "Sustainably Made in Arizona" and "Eco-Fashion" are used to describe the output, and reversible two-in-one designs are highlighted as a differentiating feature. No specific certifications, equipment lists, or tolerance standards are disclosed.

name: Yachiyo
old_description: As a world-class manufacturer of automotive parts, Motherson Yachiyo of America is committed to meeting every expectation of our customers. Our specialty is designing and producing plastic fuel tanks and sunroofs. At every turn, we work to improve our processes as we achieve the ideal outcome for our customers.
about:
Motherson Yachiyo Automotive Tech Products of America, Inc. operates from Columbus, Ohio. The U.S. subsidiary was founded in 1997 to serve the North American market, building on a parent company established in 1947 by Eiichi Otake in Japan. In 2024, Yachiyo became part of the Motherson group, expanding its global footprint.

The company designs and manufactures plastic fuel tanks and sunroof systems for automotive applications. Its capabilities span research and development, design, testing, manufacturing operations, glass encapsulation, electrodeposition (E-Coat) coating, blow molding, and final assembly. Additional product lines include power rollshades and power rear slide windows. As a Tier 1 supplier, it manages projects from conception through production.

Motherson Yachiyo of America serves the automotive industry as a Tier 1 supplier, providing components to vehicle manufacturers. Its customer base consists of automotive OEMs requiring fuel system components and sunroof modules, though specific client names are not disclosed.

The company states its goal is to become one of the world's top-level manufacturers of automotive body parts, delivering superior quality while maintaining economical products in direct response to customer needs. It differentiates itself by overseeing the full product lifecycle — R&D, testing, and manufacturing — under one roof.

name: Yarrington Mills Corporation
old_description: FE510MF 84% MicroPoly/16% Spandex Ultra Light Performance Body Flex®
about:
Yarrington Mills Corporation operates from Hatboro, Pennsylvania, where it produces performance fabrics for athletic apparel. The company’s founding year and ownership structure are not publicly disclosed.

The mill manufactures a broad range of knit and woven fabrics engineered for sportswear. Its portfolio includes spandex-blend series such as Body Flex® and Power Stretch, polyester performance knits (doubleknit, mock mesh, pique, fleece), Duraknit® nylon doubleknits, and a variety of mesh and high-luster tricot fabrics. The company also supplies rib knit trims, braid trims, elastics, and uniform braids, cords, and laces, along with finished components like jacket cuffs, collars, waistbands, and polo shirt collars.

Yarrington Mills serves the team sports market, providing fabrics for baseball and softball, basketball, cheer and dance, lacrosse, soccer, wrestling, track and field, volleyball, and jackets and warm‑ups. Its sublimation-ready fabrics support custom printing for uniforms and fan gear.

The company emphasizes a comprehensive fabric portfolio tailored to the performance demands of team sports, though it does not publish a formal mission statement or founding narrative.

name: Yearwood Performance Center
old_description: Browse Our Aftermarket Parts and Racing Fuels in Albuquerque, NM
about:
Yearwood Performance Center operates from Albuquerque, New Mexico, where it was established in 1968 as a jobber house supplying performance parts to the Southwest's hot rod community. The business has remained a fixture in the region's automotive aftermarket for over five decades.

The company maintains 8,000 square feet of combined retail and warehouse space stocked with aftermarket performance components and racing fuels. Its product range spans air intakes, camshafts and valvetrain, Edelbrock engine components, fuel delivery systems, gauges, ignition systems, nitrous oxide fuel delivery, automatic transmissions, and fuel injection systems. Yearwood conducts both retail counter sales and wholesale distribution to other retailers and shops.

The customer base centers on automotive performance enthusiasts, hot rod builders, and racers throughout New Mexico, with the shop serving Albuquerque, Rio Rancho, Meadow Lake, Cedar Crest, and surrounding areas. Its wholesale channel extends the reach to other speed shops and installers in the region.

Yearwood positions itself as New Mexico's oldest and largest speed shop, a distinction rooted in its 1968 founding and continuous operation as a combined retail and wholesale outlet for "go fast" parts.

name: Yes-Tech (Your Electronic Supplier)
old_description: How to find a second source that meets your need for delivery and price to back up the component you can’t get.
about:
Yes-Tech operates from Lake Elmo, Minnesota, as a distributor and service provider for electronic components. The company does not publish a founding year or ownership structure on its website.

The firm stocks a broad line of electronic hardware from more than two dozen manufacturers, including American Bright, Nichicon, Stackpole Electronics, and Suntsu. Product categories span LEDs, connectors, crystals and oscillators, discrete semiconductors, capacitors, resistors, diodes, and inductors. In addition to component distribution, Yes-Tech offers outsourcing services for routine production tasks such as cutting header strips to length, aiming to reduce shop-floor labor for its customers.

The company targets U.S.-based manufacturers and contract assemblers that face rising component costs and extended lead times. By acting as a second source and maintaining stocked options, Yes-Tech helps buyers manage supply-chain risk and control purchasing expenses.

Yes-Tech's stated differentiation rests on providing curated component options and then holding inventory for those selections, combined with a focus on identifying small, repetitive production jobs that can be moved off the customer's floor to lower overall cost.

name: Yoders Woodworks
old_description: Welcome to Alabama's Leading Portable Building and Storage Solution Experts!
about:
Yoders Woodworks operates from Falkville, Alabama, where it was established over 25 years ago with a mission to bring unparalleled craftsmanship to domestic and commercial markets. The company’s founders are not named publicly, and ownership details such as family or veteran status are not disclosed.

The business designs, builds, and delivers a broad line of portable structures, including storage buildings, cabins, tiny houses, garages, carports, barns, greenhouses, utility sheds, and storm shelters. It also installs metal roofs and offers fully custom builds. Work is performed by skilled carpenters using wood and metal materials, and the company maintains its own fleet for delivery and on-site placement. No facility size, headcount, or production volumes are published.

Customers range from homeowners needing backyard storage to farmers requiring livestock barns, gardeners seeking greenhouses, and vehicle owners looking for garages or carports. The company serves residential and commercial clients across Alabama and surrounding areas, with past projects including custom-sized sheds, painted wooden units with tin roofs, and reinforced entry steps.

Yoders Woodworks emphasizes durability and function over aesthetics alone, backing its work with free estimates, discounts for military personnel and first responders, and workmanship warranties. Flexible payment options such as rent-to-own and installment plans are offered, and the company states that its custom services are designed to exceed client expectations.

name: Young Wholesale Parts
about:
Young Wholesale Parts operates from Layton, Utah, serving the Intermountain West with a focus on original-equipment automotive parts. The company does not disclose its founding year or ownership structure, and no founders are named in public materials.

The distributor stocks more than 30,000 part numbers across 21 vehicle lines, including GM, Ford, Mopar, Toyota, Honda, Subaru, Kia, Hyundai, Genesis, Mazda, Volkswagen, Audi, and Nissan. Its warehouse consolidates individual carlines under one roof, and the company runs its own fleet of delivery trucks covering a corridor from Payson, Utah, to Preston, Idaho, while also offering nationwide shipping.

Primary customers are independent repair shops, collision centers, and fleet operators throughout Utah, Idaho, Montana, Nevada, Colorado, and Wyoming. A dedicated claims department handles warranty and repair paperwork, and an automated returns system powered by Elite Extra streamlines credit memos and tracking.

Young Wholesale Parts emphasizes breadth of inventory and logistical control as its differentiators: same-day access to a wide range of OE parts, direct delivery with company drivers, and integrated claims and returns support reduce downtime for shop customers.
